scope.flow: StakingNativeToken._withdraw() balance accounting during ETH transfers with reentrant claim() for a different owned service
scope.environment: Solidity staking contract (StakingBase/StakingNativeToken) with native ETH transfers and ServiceOwner reward distribution

statements.text: Attacker owns two services A and B, both staked in the same StakingNativeToken contract with RewardDistributionType.ServiceOwner.
Contract balance is 100 ETH before the outer _withdraw() executes.
Neither _claim(), _unstake(), _withdraw(), nor _stake() have reentrancy guards, and the line 564 comment only prevents re-claiming the same service.
Attacker calls unstake(serviceA), triggering the outer _withdraw().
Attacker's receive() triggers during the ETH transfer and calls claim(serviceB), invoking the inner _withdraw().

_withdraw() reads balance into a local variable, performs external ETH transfers, and writes the updated balance back only after all transfers complete, so the outer _withdraw() overwrites the inner write with its own stale local variable.
The balance state variable must be updated in storage before each external ETH transfer, not after the transfer loop, so reentrant calls cannot read a stale balance.
_withdraw, _claim, _unstake, and _stake must be protected by a reentrancy guard so reentrant calls during transfers cannot corrupt balance accounting.
The recorded balance must not exceed the actual ETH held by the contract after withdrawals complete.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the attacker's receive() is a contract or EOA; reentrancy requires a contract recipient.
Report does not specify the exact reward amounts for serviceA and serviceB beyond the illustrative 5 ETH each.
Report does not establish a prior transaction history beyond the initial balance=100 ETH state.
